title: What Lazy Days of Summer?
summary: For most of the United States, this past week saw one of the seasonal characteristics of summer- a brutal heat wave. This follows on from the heat wave that gripped Europe a few weeks ago. While most things slow to an easy pace during this weather, the tanker market, refinery operations and those that work in the industry are realizing that there may not be any "lazy days of summer" this year.

children.title: Up and Running
children.summary: refiners have been aggressively restoring capacity since outages resulting from the past hurricane season. Refinery utilization has now consistently been over 90% for two months, levels not seen since a year ago August.

children.title: % Utilization
children.summary: Today, refineries are currently processing over 17.3 million barrels per day of crude, higher than the average operating capacity for 2005 of 16.6 million barrels per day and better than the average for 2004 of 16.8 million barrels per day. Products Craze Even with refinery capacity at relative highs as compared to the last year, the demand for imported products is still very strong.
